title: Does trimming sync windows by their distance from the fitted clock line, with no tuned threshold, beat the peak-sharpness gate on real audio?
summary: Follow-up to capture-syncgate. Drops GCC windows more than 2–20 ms off a Theil-Sen clock line (up to 3 rounds), a threshold in time rather than in peak sharpness, over 10 real LibreOffice gallery clips (4 cameras, 12 windows, ±40 ppm, 12 seeds). At 0 dB SNR with gamma 0.25 the share of cuts jumping over a frame falls from 1.4% to 0.9% for any tolerance in the range, mostly from one clip (untie). At −10 dB it helps little (46.1% vs 47.6% ungated) where the PSR gate gets 37.8%; combined 37.4%. It does not fix the held-out gamma-choice failure from capture-syncgate (9.9%). Limits: ten clips from one gallery, synthetic delay and white noise, assumed clock rates, small grids, assumed one-frame criterion.
lede: does a clip-free residual-from-the-clock-line trim beat the PSR gate? At 0 dB a little (1.4% to 0.9% of cuts over a frame); at -10 dB no (46% vs 38% for PSR).
